# source: conformance/scenarios/wildcards.txt

scenario wildcards/star-matches-within-segment
kind normative
spec An asterisk matches anything except a slash.
file .gitignore
| *.log
| a*z
path debug.log => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*.log
path .log => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*.log
path dir/debug.log => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*.log
path debug.log.bak => NONE
path az => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:a*z
path abz => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:a*z
path a/z => NONE
path a/bz => NONE
path abcz/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:a*z
path a-z.txt => NONE

scenario wildcards/star-does-not-cross-slash
kind normative
spec An asterisk matches anything except a slash, so a pattern containing a slash stays within each segment.
file .gitignore
| doc/*.md
path doc/a.md => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:doc/*.md
path doc/sub/a.md => NONE
path other/doc/a.md => NONE
path doc/.md => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:doc/*.md
path doc/ => NONE

scenario wildcards/star-alone
kind normative
spec A lone asterisk matches every name at any level.
file .gitignore
| *
path a => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*
path a/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*
path .hidden => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*
path dir/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*
path dir/nested/file => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*

scenario wildcards/question-mark
kind normative
spec The character ? matches any one character except a slash.
file .gitignore
| file?.txt
| ?
path file1.txt => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:file?.txt
path file.txt => NONE
path file12.txt => NONE
path file/.txt => NONE
path x => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:?
path xy => NONE
path dir/x => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:?
path dir/xy => NONE

scenario wildcards/question-mark-not-slash
kind normative
spec The character ? matches any one character except a slash.
file .gitignore
| a?b
path a-b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a?b
path a/b => NONE
path aab => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a?b
path ab => NONE

scenario wildcards/double-star-leading
kind normative
spec A leading "**" followed by a slash means match in all directories.
file .gitignore
| **/foo
path foo => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/foo
path a/foo => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/foo
path a/b/foo => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/foo
path foo/bar => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/foo
path a/foo/bar => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/foo
path xfoo => NONE
path a/xfoo => NONE

scenario wildcards/double-star-leading-with-path
kind normative
spec A leading "**" followed by a slash means match in all directories. For example, "**/foo/bar" matches the file or directory "bar" anywhere that is directly under directory "foo".
file .gitignore
| **/foo/bar
path foo/bar => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/foo/bar
path a/foo/bar => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/foo/bar
path a/b/foo/bar => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/foo/bar
path foo/baz/bar => NONE
path foo/bar/baz => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/foo/bar
path bar => NONE

scenario wildcards/double-star-trailing
kind normative
spec A trailing "/**" matches everything inside. For example, "abc/**" matches all files inside directory "abc", relative to the location of the .gitignore file, with infinite depth.
file .gitignore
| abc/**
path abc => NONE
path abc/ => NONE
path abc/x => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:abc/**
path abc/x/y => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:abc/**
path abc/x/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:abc/**
path other/abc/x => NONE
path abcd/x => NONE

scenario wildcards/double-star-middle
kind normative
spec A slash followed by two consecutive asterisks then a slash matches zero or more directories. For example, "a/**/b" matches "a/b", "a/x/b", "a/x/y/b" and so on.
file .gitignore
| a/**/b
path a/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/**/b
path a/x/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/**/b
path a/x/y/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/**/b
path a/x/y/z/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/**/b
path a/xb => NONE
path ab => NONE
path x/a/b => NONE
path a/b/c => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/**/b
path a/x/b/c => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/**/b

scenario wildcards/double-star-both-ends
kind normative
spec A leading "**" followed by a slash means match in all directories. A trailing "/**" matches everything inside.
file .gitignore
| **/cache/**
path cache => NONE
path cache/ => NONE
path cache/a => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/cache/**
path x/cache/a => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/cache/**
path x/y/cache/a/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/cache/**
path x/cache => NONE
path mycache/a => NONE

scenario wildcards/double-star-only
kind normative
spec A lone "**" is a wildcard pattern like any other and behaves as the one-segment pattern "*" at any depth.
file .gitignore
| **
path a => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**
path a/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**
path a/b/c => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**
path .x => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**

scenario wildcards/double-star-adjacent-text
kind normative
spec Other consecutive asterisks are considered regular asterisks and will match according to the previous rules.
file .gitignore
| a**b
| c/x**
| **y/d
path ab => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a**b
path a-b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a**b
path a/b => NONE
path axxb => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a**b
path c/x => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c/x**
path c/xyz => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c/x**
path c/x/y => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c/x**
path zy/d => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:**y/d
path y/d => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:**y/d
path a/zy/d => NONE
path z/y/d => NONE

scenario wildcards/triple-star
kind git-quirk
spec Other consecutive asterisks are considered regular asterisks, but runs of three are not covered by an example.
note Git lets "a/***/b" span several directories, so it does not treat the run as a plain asterisk.
file .gitignore
| a/***/b
| ***.tmp
path a/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/***/b
path a/x/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/***/b
path a/x/y/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/***/b
path x.tmp => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:***.tmp
path d/x.tmp => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:***.tmp

scenario wildcards/star-mixed-with-double-star
kind normative
spec A slash followed by two consecutive asterisks then a slash matches zero or more directories.
file .gitignore
| src/**/*.gen.kt
path src/A.gen.kt => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:src/**/*.gen.kt
path src/a/A.gen.kt => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:src/**/*.gen.kt
path src/a/b/A.gen.kt => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:src/**/*.gen.kt
path src/A.kt => NONE
path other/src/A.gen.kt => NONE
path src/gen.kt => NONE
